answer: What I'd add is an appeal ladder. If a seller thinks a grading result got rigged, it can bump the job up a rung, and the next panel is twice as big and made only of accounts that didn't sit on the last one. Say a farm swings a 5-seat vote on a cedar deck inspection. The appeal goes to 10, then 20, then 40. Winning once is cheap. Keeping the win means owning a majority of a bigger and bigger crowd, and near the top that's most of the active graders. If a falcon nesting survey verdict flips, the payout delta goes back to the seller and the clones lose their grading seats.
